claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is the environment variable specifying the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset, the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud; a separate domain is not required.
The state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, login commands, and TF_TOKEN_* variable name.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ describing the Terraform state backend.
The TF_TOKEN_* environment variable name incorporates the domain value, and `terraform login` / `tofu login` accept the domain for the Pulumi Cloud Terraform-compatible API.
